newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close up after touching new high.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close up after touching new high.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended up on Tuesday after touching a new high of 691.49 points on the back of institutional buying in certain heavyweights, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index closed up 4.99 points, or 0.73 percent, at 689.97 points after hitting a record 691.49 points. The previous record of 688.48 was reached on January 23.
Gainers led losers by 73 to 56, with 56 issues unchanged. Total volume was 249.3 million shares on a turnover of 468.1 billion rupiah.
An analyst with a Singapore-based securities firm said the market was strong enough to make further gains on Wednesday.

Brokers predicted the higher closing price of heavyweight Telkom in Jakarta could trigger a further rise in New York. Telkom was up 75 to 4,200 rupiah on a volume of 5.6 million shares, against $34-3/8 in New York overnight.

Brokers also said a report Telkom planned to invest around 4.3 trillion rupiah in the 1997/98 fiscal year starting April 1, down from 4.5 trillion rupiah in fiscal 1996/97, could boost sentiment in the stock.
"From a technical aspect, I expect the market should face some correction this week. But for the last two days, that assumption has not applied," the analyst said.
He attributed Tuesday's gains to strong demand from regional buyers in certain heavyweight counters, including Telkom, Semen Gresik and Sampoerna.
"I believe some investors from Hongkong and Singapore were shifting or adding weighting to their Indonesia portfolio," he said.
Brokers and analysts believed a report on Monday from Thornton Management (Asia) Ltd had had a positive impact on the Jakarta bourse.
Thornton said it had reduced its weighting in the Hong Kong stock market to about 35 percent of its US$1.5 billion Asia-ex-Japan portfolio from about 40 percent.
The portfolio had been reweighted in favour of the Jakarta Stock Exchange, where a declining interest rate environment had created a positive near-term outlook, Thornton said.
Cigarette maker Sampoerna rose 2.11 percent to 14,500 rupiah on a volume of 633,500 shares on foreign buying, brokers said.

Well-diversified Bakrie & Brothers topped the active list with 21.6 million shares traded, rising 100 rupiah to 1,175 rupiah on continued speculation the firm might sell its stake in Freeport Indonesia, which operates one of the world's largest gold and copper mines in Irian Jaya.
"So far, no decision has been made on that matter," Suresh Kumar, Bakrie's investor relations, said. He declined to give further comment.
